notes: Four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) via background subagents covering 2026-10-08/09. anthropic.com/news was directly fetchable and surfaced three genuine same-day announcements (Usage Policy update, Genesis Mission commitment, Cyber Mission launch); every other vendor domain (openai.com, developers.openai.com, weforum.org, ces.tech, aws.amazon.com, cisa.gov, govdelivery.com) hit routine ENOTFOUND/EGRESS_BLOCKED and was worked around via WebSearch. Same-day coverage for Oct 8-9 was otherwise thin to the point of index lag (security lane: nothing in the index past Oct 7; devtools/cloud: no indexed same-day primary-source posts at all), so this run leans on the three Anthropic items plus a handful of forward-looking corrections. Many forward-looking candidates the lanes turned up (CES 2027, MWC Barcelona 2027, NVIDIA GTC 2027, ICLR 2027, WEF Davos 2027, Amazon Bedrock Claude Opus 4.1 retirement, Azure AI Foundry GPT-5 retirement, AWS re:Invent 2026, Microsoft Ignite 2026, KubeCon Europe 2027, Amazon EKS 1.32 extended support, Broadcom Q4 FY2026 earnings) were cross-checked against the existing corpus and turned out to already be filed at equal or better confidence, so they were deliberately not re-filed. Dropped several purely speculative, single-countdown-site 'rumored' earnings/launch guesses (Microsoft/Meta/Apple fiscal-quarter earnings projections, Galaxy S27 Unpacked, Google I/O 2027) and two items with genuinely conflicting dates across sources (AWS Lambda Node.js 18.x full block timeline, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS EOL day) rather than guess between them.
concerns: data/events/2027-04.json carries TWO active entries for the same conference, both titled exactly 'ICLR 2027', same dates (2027-04-26 to 2027-04-30), same venue claim conflict (one says Moscone Center SF, the other says venue unconfirmed): ids 'iclr-2027-2027-04' (firstSeen 2026-08-20) and 'international-conference-on-learning-representations-iclr-20-2027-04' (firstSeen 2026-10-08, added by yesterday's run). This is the slug-truncation / id-collision issue flagged in prior runs' concerns (src/lib/id.ts's title-to-id slugging truncates long titles before the sameTitle comparison runs, so a title that reads identically after truncation on one side but not the other can create two ids for one real-world event) — now confirmed as live duplicate data, not just a risk. A maintainer should merge these two rows into one and keep the better-sourced summary (the first one cites iclr.cc/Conferences/2027/CallForPapers and names Moscone Center SF; the second cites only iclr.cc/Conferences/2027/Dates and says venue unconfirmed — the first looks more complete).

The AI lane's search snippets kept surfacing an OpenAI model called 'GPT-6.1 Astra', reported (WSJ via Reuters/AFP, ~Sept 28 2026) as shelved/cancelled before shipping over safety concerns. This is a different, distinct thing from the already-filed 'OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast goes live on NVIDIA Blackwell' (2026-10-01) — one is cancelled, the other shipped — but the names are a one-digit version-number apart, which is exactly the pattern that has caused this repo's fuzzy-dedupe (sameTitle, 0.6 Jaccard floor, no version-number special-casing) to silently collapse distinct entries in past runs. Not filing the cancellation itself (not calendar-worthy, no future date), but flagging in case a future run's finding about 'GPT-6.1 Astra' gets merged onto the wrong existing row.
